{{Short description|American physicist}}
'''Robert P. Behringer''' (October 26, 1948 – July 10, 2018) was an American [[physicist]]<ref name="duke.edu">{{cite web|url=https://scholars.duke.edu/display/per9697242|title=Behringer, Robert P. |publisher=duke.edu |access-date=May 30, 2017}}</ref> based at [[Duke University]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/200304/lobbying.cfm |title=Lobbying |publisher=aps.org |access-date=May 30, 2017}}</ref> whose research first dealt with [[critical phenomena]] and transport properties in fluid [[helium]], such as [[Rayleigh–Bénard convection]], and  since 1986 was involved with [[granular material]], where his most notable achievements were in the development of the technique of [[photoelasticity]] to study spatio-temporal fluctuations. This enabled him to extract vector forces from images of photo-elastic disks, which are models for granular materials. His research demonstrated the strongly fluctuating nature of granular flows. Another aspect of his research involved the concept of jamming in granular materials.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://meetings.aps.org/Meeting/DFD16/Session/A30?showAbstract |title=Sessions |volume=61 |issue=20 |publisher=aps.org |access-date=May 30, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://meetings.aps.org/Meeting/MAR17/Session/A14.11 |title=Sessions |volume=62 |issue=4 |publisher=aps.org |access-date=May 30, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&q=Robert+Behringer&btnG=&as_sdt=1%2C44&as_sdtp= |title=Robert Behringer |access-date=May 30, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://jamming.research.yale.edu/news.html |title=Yale News |publisher=yale.edu |access-date=May 30, 2017}}</ref>

A native of [[Baltimore]] and the son of Frederick and Elizabeth Behringer, he obtained his BSc in Physics at Duke University in 1970, his PhD in Physics in 1975 also at Duke University, with [[Horst Meyer (physicist)|Horst Meyer]] as his mentor, and was a research associate at [[Bell Labs]] under the direction of Guenter Ahlers from 1975 -77. A faculty position at [[Wesleyan University]] was the next step and in 1982 he was appointed by Duke University, where he became a [[James B. Duke Professor]] in 1994.<ref name="duke.edu"/>

Behringer died on July 10, 2018, aged 69.<ref>{{cite news |title=DUKE FLAGS LOWERED: PHYSICS PROFESSOR ROBERT P. BEHRINGER DIES AT 69 |url=https://today.duke.edu/2018/07/physics-professor-robert-p-behringer-dies-69 |access-date=July 12, 2023 |publisher=Duke University |date=July 11, 2018}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
*Alfred P. Sloan Foundation Fellow (1981-1985)
*Fellow, American Physical Society (1993–present)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?institution=Duke%20University&nom_unit=&year= |title=Fellows |publisher=aps.org |access-date=May 30, 2017}}</ref>
*Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science (1999–present)<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.aaas.org/fellow/behringer-robert-p |title=Robert P. Behringer |publisher=aaas.org |access-date=May 30, 2017}}</ref>
*James B. Duke Professor (1994–present)
*Visiting Scientist, Ecole Supérieure de Physique et Chimie Industrielles, Paris, 1997. 
*Joliot Curie Chair, Ecole Supérieure de Physique et Chimie Industrielles, Paris, 2010. 
*Visiting Scientist, C.E.A. Saclay, France, Fall 2010.
*Chair Line, American Physical Society Topical Group<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.aps.org/units/gpc/governance/committees.cfm |title=Committee |publisher=aps.org |access-date=May 30, 2017}}</ref> on the Physics of  Climate, American Physical Society, 2012
*{{ill|Jesse W. Beams Award|de}} of the Physical Society, South-Eastern Section, 2013
